title: Blade OML angular position at the +72 deg (high-pitch) end stop, hub A datum to blade OML, full-sweep-average sensitivity (degrees)

checks.label: Blade-pitch angular position variation margin against S461-607, at the +72 deg end stop

source_ref.callout: The pitch angle of each blade in a propeller assembly shall not exceed +/-0.5 degrees of the mean pitch of the blades
source_ref.note: c_status: draft. Pulled 2026-09-06 from Polarion (Delta mirror, manufacturing.polarion.workitem); severity must_have. Same adoption reasoning as the -7 deg study's check: a blade-to-blade variation limit used as the closest available numeric acceptance criterion, because S461-241 states only the two nominal stop angles and S461-805's own threshold is TBD.

context_ref.callout: The propeller assembly shall provide propeller pitch end stops at -7º and +72º.
context_ref.note: c_status: draft. Pulled 2026-09-06. Names the nominal operating point this study represents (+72 deg); not itself a numeric criterion, so not folded into the check.

excluded_terms: hub top deck to actuator mounting face (edge hub_top_deck_to_vpa_mount) -- no source document, `assumed` placeholder
actuator mounting face to end-stop feature (edge vpa_mount_to_end_stop_feature) -- no source document, `assumed` placeholder

piston end to end-stop feature (edge end_stop_clearance) -- THE end stop itself; a real drawing candidate exists (214700-002-A sheet 2, `5.00 +/-0.05`) but its feature identity is not established (WORKSHEET_endstop_vision_baseline.md §8b row 39, 'candidate (strong)'), so it stays `untraced`
blade root to OML (edge blade_root_clocking_to_oml) -- not a drawing quantity at all; the source workbook's own author doubts the number by roughly 6x (row 22, 'Probably closer to .03deg')

the full-sweep-average sensitivity this study borrows (transform pitch_arm_linear_to_rotary_average, source cells F10/F11) is an average over the WHOLE sweep, not a condition characterised at either end of it -- it is a materially weaker stand-in for +72 deg than the worst-case study's -5 deg constant is for -7 deg, because +72 deg is the far end of the sweep from where the sheet's worst-case column is stated. No sensitivity constant characterised AT or NEAR +72 deg exists in any source this repo holds -- this is the sharper half of the new finding this study exists to name

gas-spring bushing tipping backlash -- the source workbook's largest single angular contributor (0.72 deg, its row 68) and not represented as a chain edge at all (see this topology's own notes, 'WHAT THIS TOPOLOGY CANNOT REPRODUCE')

S461-805 (Blade Pitch Position Accuracy) states its own threshold as literally 'TBD deg' in Polarion -- draft, no usable numeric criterion, so it supplies no check of its own and is not folded into this one either

checks.label: Blade-pitch angular position variation margin against the operating/hard-stop design margin (S461-617), at the +72 deg end stop

source_ref.callout: Derived, not quoted: S461-241 ('The propeller assembly shall provide propeller pitch end stops at -7º and +72º') gives a total mechanical-stop span of 79 deg; S461-516/637 ('The Gas Spring will have a nominal normal operating stroke of 61.67 mm. Note: The operating stroke is equivalent to 75° blade pitch travel.') gives a 75 deg normal operating range. Margin = 79 - 75 = 4 deg.
source_ref.note: c_status: draft (S461-241) / validated (S461-516/637) -- mixed, named as such. Pulled 2026-09-06 from Polarion. `inferred` per SOP Step 5b: derived from two directly-quoted requirement figures, with the derivation written out above. Added by handoff `mechanical_stroke_stack`, 2026-09-06, appended to this study's pre-existing `checks` list -- see this study's own `selection`/`transforms`, unchanged from the day this file was authored. Same derivation as the -7 deg study's twin check -- one total margin, applied at both stops (see excluded_terms).

context_ref.callout: The mechanical stroke between travel stops shall be defined with sufficient tolerance to ensure that contact with the mechanical stops during normal closed-loop operation is extremely improbable
context_ref.note: c_status: validated. Pulled 2026-09-06. States no number of its own -- the requirement this check exists to answer, using a limit derived from S461-241/S461-516 rather than quoted from this cell. Byte-identical duplicate: S461-639.

excluded_terms: the same model gaps `s461_607_margin_at_plus72` names above (the two `assumed` placeholders, the end stop's own unresolved feature identity, the doubted blade-root-to-OML estimate, and the full-sweep-average sensitivity being the weakest available stand-in for either stop) apply here unchanged -- this check folds the identical study total, only the limit differs
gas-spring bushing tipping backlash -- unmodelled in this chain (see this topology's own notes, 'WHAT THIS TOPOLOGY CANNOT REPRODUCE')

the limit assumes S461-241/S461-516's 4 deg margin is available in full at THIS stop specifically; neither requirement states how the margin splits between -7 deg and +72 deg, so an uneven split could leave less than 4 deg here
the limit rests in part on S461-241, which is `c_status: draft`

provenance.why_this_study_exists: S461-241 (draft, 'End stop') requires the propeller assembly to provide pitch end stops at -7 deg and +72 deg. This study pairs with study_pitch_system_end_stop_minus7.json for the high-pitch side, per the handoff's item 1 ('one study per stop direction'). Its selection and transform set are `pitch_system_blade_angle_average`'s exact contents, re-titled and re-scoped -- a SEPARATE document, not an edit of that one, for the same reason the -7 deg study is separate: the handoff's baseline forbids touching the four existing pitch-system study documents' numbers.
provenance.the_condition_mismatch_named_and_sharper: The -7 deg study at least borrows a sensitivity the source sheet characterises near one end of the sweep (-5 deg, 2 deg off). This study has no such thing to borrow: the only other constant the sheet gives is a full-sweep AVERAGE (F10/F11), which is not characterised at either end, and +72 deg is the far end from where the worst-case column sits. Using it here is the least-bad available choice, not a good one, and it is named as such rather than presented as equivalent in quality to the -7 deg study's approximation.

notes: Selection and transforms are byte-for-byte identical to study_pitch_system_blade_angle_average.json's; only the id, title, provenance and the added `checks` entry differ. Verified by tests/test_topology.py::test_an_end_stop_study_s_selection_and_transforms_equal_its_source_study[plus72-vs-average]. Comparing the two files' totals is therefore a no-op by construction -- the point of this document is the check, not a new number.

complete: false, for the same class of reasons as the -7 deg study, plus a sharper one: the full-sweep-average sensitivity is the weakest available stand-in for either end stop, and this end is the one it is furthest from characterising. That does not block publishing the number -- it is why the number renders as a budget, never a hardware verdict.
